Outlet: Reuters via Yahoo Finance, published Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:52 PM GMT
FTSE 100 posts weekly loss as AI jitters spark risk-off move

FTSE 100: fell 1.01% to 10,673.94 points; down 0.5% for the week
FTSE 250: slipped 0.80%; tiny weekly gain
S&P 500 and Nasdaq traded higher Friday after Thursday's sharpest one-day fall since April 2025
STOXX 600: ended 1% lower
Precious metal miners: rose 1.7%
Telecom stocks: dropped 3.6% (BT Group -6.4%, Airtel Africa -4%)
Pharma and personal care: slid around 0.6%; Drug and groceries: slid around 1.7%
Energy stocks: ended down 1.6%
Man Group: fell 7.6% on FTSE 250

The Democrats' capture of the US House and Senate sparked concerns about AI regulation, potential slowdown in data-centre buildouts, and hyperscalers reducing spending.

"When $2.5 trillion of value is lost from one of the major US stock market indices in a day, it's understandable that investors are feeling on edge," said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell.

Lloyds reported British house prices fell at their fastest annual pace in a year during October as elevated mortgage costs reduced demand. Kuwait's public pension fund won a lawsuit against Man Group asset manager.
